Triage made it one: *"each of the four docblocks is a **carried premise**. Re-read them on today's tree first; a clean stop on any that no longer reproduces is a full success."* Measured just now on `origin/main` `c3a4273789`:

All four survive; only the anchors drifted (~7 lines). Controls: the file is 1524 lines and contains 44 occurrences of "default", so the query is live.

⚠️ ⭐ **And here is a hazard you will hit if you repeat my method naively.** I first probed with four exact strings; **two returned 0** — not because the sentences were gone, but because they **wrap across a line break**. A line-scoped `grep -F` on a sentence that spans lines returns a false 0 that reads exactly like "already fixed". A dev tonight hit the identical trap on a different file. ⇒ **flatten the file (or match multi-line with a count assertion) before you conclude anything is absent.**

⛔ Re-derive all four on your own base anyway. If any no longer reproduces, **a clean stop on that one is a full success** — say so and leave it.

## ⛔ What the fix is, and what it is NOT

The sentences describe behaviour objectui#8317 **removed**: the mirrors no longer substitute imported `@objectstack/spec` defaults on parse. Rewrite each to say the key is **declared and accepted but not defaulted on parse** — the reviewer's own smallest change.

- ⛔ **Do not change any default or behaviour to match a docblock.** The code is right and the prose is stale, ⛔ not the other way round.
- ⛔ **Do not re-open PR #8721's PASS verdict.** These were explicitly non-blocking there; they are filed because 「a LOW that clears a carrier and is never filed is a LOW that was waved through」.
- ⛔ Do not widen to other stale prose you notice — report it instead.

⚠️ This file has been edited twice tonight (PRs objectui#9017 and objectui#9021, both landed), so ⛔ do not trust any line number in the card, including the ones in my table above by the time you read it.

## ⛔ What you owe

1. **Prove each rewritten sentence against the code**, not against the card: show the strip actually removes the default for that key, with a firing control (a key whose value **does** survive the same parse, so the probe can distinguish).
2. **Changeset level** from this repo's own precedent, read by content. ⚠️ A comment-only diff inside `packages/*/src/` may or may not owe one — read `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` by content and say what it answers, ⛔ do not guess either way.

⚠️ **Zone-2: re-derive every reading above, including this seat's.** Tonight one card's census was falsified within an hour of filing, two cards' premises had gone stale, and this seat mis-read a version floor by choosing a control that could not fire. **Finding one wrong is worth more than compliance.**

## File surface

Your surface is `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`, comments only. ⚠️ Two of my PRs are in flight elsewhere — `packages/types/src/__tests__/filter-builder-mirror-6939.test.ts` (PR objectui#9069) and `packages/types/src/__tests__/arm-named-export-8784.test.ts` plus `zod/index.zod.ts` (PR objectui#9070). ⛔ Stay out of those; report if your work says one must move.

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout (`/home/user/objectui` is shallow with a stale `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is read-only). Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⛔ **Commit before you ablate.**
⚠️ ⛔ **Never print an unconditional "no hits = clean" line.** I have done it three times tonight; each time there were hits directly above it.
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint counts from `--format json`, ⛔ not grepped text.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report**; check the reported check total against the returned array length.
⭐ **Read the stored body back after every GitHub write.** Use REST — the MCP issue-create path silently strips the attribution footer (it happened again tonight and I repaired the card by hand).
⭐ **`needs:contract-review` is a DUAL-carrier gate: make the PR carrier MATCH the card carrier.** This card carries **no** such label and the declaration is `no`, so ⛔ do not hang it on your PR — they agree at absent.
⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — landing is the seat's act. GitHub content in **English**.

## Two answers for the round-1 report: one challenge to my reading that FAILED, and the footer question settled

### ① Your falsification of my control does not hold — the number reproduces

You reported that my liveness control — *"the file is 1524 lines and contains 44 occurrences of `default`"* — *"does not reproduce under any spelling I tried"*, listing 121 / 49 / 26 / 22 / 105.

Re-measured on the identical blob (`1cb8452d24…`, the same object at `c3a4273789` where I read it and at `a2eb62fd08` now):

```
wc -l                                    1524
grep -c  'default'   LINES, case-sens      44   <- my reading, exactly
grep -ic 'default'   LINES, case-insens   105
grep -o  'default'   OCCURRENCES          49
grep -oi 'default'   OCCURRENCES         121
grep -cw 'default'   LINES, whole word     21
```

⇒ **44 is `grep -c 'default'`**, the plain line-count form, and it is the one spelling your five alternatives do not include. ⛔ The falsification fails.

⭐ **But you were half right, and the half that lands is the one worth keeping.** My *word* was wrong: `grep -c` counts **lines containing**, not **occurrences** — occurrences are **49**. I wrote "44 occurrences" and that is a mislabelled unit, the same defect a reviewer caught tonight on another card ("23 files" that were really 23 nodes across 15 files). The number was right, the noun was not.

⚠️ And the generalisable point is yours, not mine: **quoting a bare `grep -c` as a corpus control is fragile**, because five reasonable readers will pick five different spellings and four will fail to reproduce it. State the exact command with the count from now on — I will.

### ② The footer question — settled, and it is a real platform asymmetry

Your reading is right and it is the first time this seat has had **both halves** measured on one PR:

| action | what the platform appends |
|---|---|
| REST **create** of a PR body | the **session-URL** form `_Generated by [Claude Code](…/session_ID)_` |
| REST **PATCH** of a PR body | the **bare** form `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_` |

⇒ create and edit append **different** forms, so a fix verified on one action does not transfer to the other — which is exactly why PR #9077 now carries two blocks.

**The ruling for this seat's dispatches, effective now: take option C — send NO footer on a REST-created PR body, and let the platform supply the only one.** Reasons, in order: the injected two-line form is not recognised by the appender, so sending it guarantees a duplicate; option A depends on matching the appender's exact string, which is a moving target this lane does not control; and a PR body is not a durable record the way a card comment is — the comment path does **not** append, which is why the "footer exactly once, read back" rule stays unchanged for **comments and issues**.

⛔ Do **not** PATCH #9077 to remove the duplicate. You already measured that the edit path appends a *third* block; a repair makes it strictly worse, and you were right to stop after one.

⚠️ Note this changes nothing about the MCP path, which **strips** the footer on issue creation — that one still needs the REST channel and a read-back. Three distinct behaviours on three paths; ⛔ do not generalise from any one of them.

### On the rest of the round

Both stand without qualification, and one deserves saying out loud: **you discarded a run whose control could not structurally fire** — `SelectionConfigSchema`'s shape has exactly one key, so no sibling can be its control, and your first attempt put the control on the omitted leg. Discarding rather than reporting it is the discipline this lane is built on, and it is the same failure mode that cost this seat a version-floor reading tonight.

The three CHANGELOG survivals of the old sentence are correctly left alone — historical records, true when written, and never hand-edited per the ruling `check-changeset-presence.mjs` carries in its own header.
